sourcePolicy: All questions in this pack are Ready2Go original draft practice items unless an individual record states otherwise. No official JAMB past-question corpus is included. Human subject-matter and answer-key review is required before public release.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element equals the number of…
questions.explanation: Atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.question: At approximately 25°C, a solution with pH 3 is…
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 indicates an acidic solution at about 25°C.

questions.question: Which type of bond forms when atoms share a pair of electrons?
questions.explanation: A covalent bond involves shared electron pairs between atoms.

questions.question: Which method is most suitable for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid?
questions.explanation: Filtration retains the insoluble solid while the liquid passes through.

questions.question: How many moles are present in 18 g of water? (H₂O = 18 g mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 18 ÷ 18 = 1 mol.

questions.question: The atomic number of an element equals the number of what in its nucleus?
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined by proton number.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of what?
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ in neutron number.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A covalent bond forms when atoms do what?
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding involves shared electron pairs.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A solution with pH 2 is best classified as what at room temperature?
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 is acidic.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: A catalyst increases reaction rate mainly by doing what?

options.C: Changing the identity of all atoms
options.D: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy

questions.explanation: Catalysts lower the activation-energy barrier.

questions.explanation: Oxidation involves electron loss.

questions.question: Neutralisation between an acid and a base commonly produces what?
questions.explanation: Acid-base neutralisation generally forms salt and water.

questions.question: Which change of state converts a liquid to a gas throughout the liquid at its boiling point?
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs when vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.question: Which method is best for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid?

questions.question: At constant temperature, pressure of a fixed amount of gas is inversely proportional to volume under which idealised law?
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law relates pressure and volume inversely at constant temperature.
questions.authoringNote: Original draft created for product testing; requires qualified subject review.

questions.question: Oxidation occurs at which electrode in an electrochemical cell?
questions.explanation: Oxidation is defined at the anode.

questions.question: The functional group of alcohols is which?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain a hydroxyl group attached to carbon.

questions.question: Molar concentration is typically expressed as what?

options.A: Atoms per kilogram of solvent only
options.B: Moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution
options.D: Litres per mole of gas only

questions.explanation: Molar concentration is amount of substance divided by solution volume.
